props.title: René Moffatt
props.face: His own songs and covers, solo or with his band.
props.lede: You know that moment at a party when someone picks up a guitar and sings a song they wrote? That’s what René Moffatt does, and his folk and Americana songs would sit nicely on a playlist with Josh Ritter and The Avett Brothers. He’s a lovely choice for welcome drinks, a patio party or a dinner where you’d like people to listen, and he can bring his band, René Moffatt & The Moonshadows, when you want a bigger sound.
props.headingNote: We can plan the music around your event, from how many musicians René brings to the songs and what everyone wears. Here’s how booking through Signet works.

props.title: René Moffatt playing his own song Hope For Better Things on voice and acoustic guitar

props.html: He’s based just outside Denver and has six records to his name, including King of the Mountain and Here and Now Is Home, and he’s entered the NPR Tiny Desk Contest every year since 2019. He calls his music heady folk for the open-hearted.

On his own, he’s played places around Denver where people come just for the songs, such as Swallow Hill and the Black Rose Acoustic Society, and he’s also performed at the Denver Botanic Gardens and the Clyfford Still Museum. His band adds lead guitar, bass and drums to those same songs. They’ve played the Boulder Roots Music Fest, and you can watch them in the video clips below.

rows.text: René can play your ceremony with just his voice and an acoustic guitar, then stay on for the cocktail hour and keep things quiet enough for everyone to catch up. It sounds like one person singing to the people in front of him, and he can play his own songs, covers or a mix of both.
René can play solo or with his trio after a long day of sessions, quietly enough for people to talk, and his songs are worth stopping to hear.
He’s a great fit for a home, especially if you’d like your guests to sit and listen to the songs. Indoors, we’d usually suggest René solo, and the trio works well in a backyard.

He’s a featured artist in the Denver Public Library’s Volume Denver program. That makes him a natural fit for a library or a farmers market on his own, and his band can play a park stage for a city’s summer series. Send us the call for performers and we’ll suggest the right size.

props.html: Working out how the music fits around the speeches? Our run of show planner can help, and our cost guide gives a general view of what live music costs across Colorado.

items.q: Does he play covers at a private event?
items.a: Yes, he mixes them in with his own songs. He can lean toward the songs your guests already know or toward his own, so just let us know the balance you'd like.

Solo, it's just a voice and a guitar, so it stays soft, and anyone who wants to listen can still hear every word. The full band has drums, so it's louder, and it's a better fit for a bigger crowd. He can adjust the volume to suit your venue and your guests.
Yes, on his own or with the band. Let us know about your venue and we can help you decide.
